outcome: No proof, disproof or general reduction of Tutte's 5-flow conjecture has been posted since 26 January 2024, and every source that states a status (Wikipedia's Nowhere-zero flow article, the 2026 papers that discuss it, the Matroid Union and Oum expositions) still calls it open. In the window there is one restricted-class result (Li and Su, 2025: every bridgeless graph of Euler genus at most 20 has a nowhere-zero 5-flow), several 2026 papers on routes through Jain's unit-vector-flow conjectures (one of which refutes Jain's S2 labelling conjecture by computer-verified counterexamples, which bears on one implying route but not on Tutte's conjecture itself), and neighbouring-problem events that are AI-linked (an AlphaEvolve-found example on a reconfiguration analogue, and OpenAI's GPT 5.6 cycle-double-cover proof claim), none of which settles this statement.
problem_asks: Read from the statement alone: for every bridgeless graph G (no bound on order, connectivity, genus or cyclic structure is stated), G admits a nowhere-zero 5-flow, meaning an orientation together with an assignment of a nonzero value from {1,2,3,4} (or equivalently a nonzero element of Z5 with the flow sign convention) to each edge such that the net flow at every vertex is zero. Parts: (a) one universal quantifier over all bridgeless graphs; (b) the single existence conclusion for each. Nothing else is asked. The bullet sits under Tutte's conjectures; its parent bullet also lists the 4-flow conjecture for Petersen-minor-free bridgeless graphs, which this bullet does not ask about.

events.what_happened: Kilpatrick (Cape Town thesis, 1975 per search summary) and Jaeger (J. Combin. Theory Ser. B, 1979, 'Flows and generalized coloring theorems in graphs') independently proved that every bridgeless graph has a nowhere-zero 8-flow. The Illinois open-problem page states this as 'Kilpatrick and Jaeger proved that every bridgeless graph is 8-flowable'. This is a weaker bound than the 5-flow statement, so it establishes a bound on the problem and nothing of the conjectured value.
events.delivers: Every bridgeless graph has a nowhere-zero 8-flow. Restricted to the weaker value 8; no case of the value 5 is settled.
events.remains: The whole statement: existence of a nowhere-zero 5-flow for every bridgeless graph.

checked_by.qualification: Published in JCTB, a refereed journal (Jaeger); thesis (Kilpatrick)
checked_by.what_they_did: Proved the 8-flow theorem; the Illinois open-problem page cites it as a known result

events.direction: Supports the conjecture only in the weaker form (8 rather than 5). Does not cut against it.

events.what_happened: Seymour, 'Nowhere-zero 6-flows', J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 30 (1981) 130-135: every bridgeless graph has a nowhere-zero 6-flow. Both the Illinois page and the Mohar problem page cite this as the best general bound. Later short proofs (DeVos-Rollova-Samal arXiv 1512.06214, 2015; DeVos-Nurse arXiv 2307.04768, 2023; DeVos-McDonald-Nurse arXiv 2302.08625) prove the 6-flow theorem itself and are not new results on the 5-flow statement.
events.delivers: Every bridgeless graph has a nowhere-zero 6-flow. A weaker value; no 5-flow case.

checked_by.qualification: Refereed journal publication; the result has been reproved in several papers
checked_by.what_they_did: Published proof; later short proofs by DeVos, Rollova, Samal, Nurse and McDonald (search summaries, not opened)

events.direction: Supports only the weaker 6-flow statement; does not cut against the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Steinberg, 'Tutte's 5-flow conjecture for the projective plane', J. Graph Theory 8 (1984) 277-289: the 5-flow statement is proved for graphs embeddable in the real projective plane. The Illinois page gives this as a known partial result.
events.delivers: Restricted class: bridgeless graphs embeddable in the projective plane have a nowhere-zero 5-flow. Settles that class completely (within the statement's scope for that class) but not graphs of higher or nonorientable-surface genus.
events.remains: Every bridgeless graph not embeddable in the projective plane.

checked_by.who: Steinberg; J. Graph Theory (journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published proof for the projective-plane class

events.direction: Proves the statement for a restricted class (projective-planar graphs); consistent with the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Kochol, Acta Mathematica Universitatis Comenianae 68 (1999) pp. 249-252 (search summaries; EMIS page returned HTTP 503, so not opened): bridgeless cubic graphs with no Petersen minor have a nowhere-zero 5-flow. Other Kochol results are cited by secondary sources with differing dates: a reduction showing that a minimum counterexample to the 5-flow statement is a cyclically 6-edge-connected cubic graph (cited as 2002 and as 2004 in different sources; Mazzuoccolo-Steffen cite 2004), and a girth bound of at least 9 for minimum counterexamples (Combinatorica, DOI 10.1007/s00493-006-0006-1, suggesting 2006). The dates of the reduction and girth results are not settled by what I could read.
events.delivers: Restricted class: bridgeless cubic graphs with no Petersen minor have a nowhere-zero 5-flow. Separately, the reduction shows the statement is equivalent to its restriction to cyclically 6-edge-connected cubic graphs; the girth bound constrains a minimum counterexample but does not settle the statement.
events.remains: Cubic bridgeless graphs containing a Petersen minor; and the reduced cyclically 6-edge-connected cubic case in general.

checked_by.who: Kochol; journal of record (Acta Math. Univ. Comenianae, Combinatorica)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the restricted-class result and the reduction (search summaries; not opened)

events.doubts: Not read: the EMIS record returned HTTP 503 and the Combinatorica record was not opened, so the statements and dates are from search summaries.
events.direction: Restricted-class support and a reduction; consistent with the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Steffen, 'Tutte's 5-flow conjecture for graphs of non-orientable genus 5', J. Graph Theory 22 (1996) 309-319. Bibliographic record from the Paderborn repository (search result); the paper was not opened.
events.delivers: Per its title, a restricted class: graphs of nonorientable genus 5 (Euler genus 5 in the sense of the title). The content was not read, so the exact scope is taken from the title.
events.remains: Graphs of other genus and the general statement.

checked_by.who: Steffen; J. Graph Theory (journal of record)

events.doubts: Content not read; the scope is inferred from the title and from the Li-Su reference list, which cites it.
events.direction: Restricted-class support if the title is accurate; consistent with the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Steffen, 'Tutte's 5-Flow Conjecture for Highly Cyclically Connected Cubic Graphs', arXiv math/0607077 (v1 submitted 4 July 2006; v2 20 Sep 2012); journal reference Discrete Math. 310 (2010) 385-389. The paper shows that a cubic graph has a nowhere-zero 5-flow if no edge cut with fewer than a certain number of edges separates two odd cycles of a minimum 2-factor, and corollary: if the graph is cyclically n-edge-connected with n >= (5/2)omega - 1 (omega the oddness), it has a nowhere-zero 5-flow.
events.delivers: Restricted class: cubic graphs with cyclic edge-connectivity n >= (5/2)omega - 1, where omega is the oddness. The statement is settled for that class only.
events.remains: Cubic bridgeless graphs whose cyclic edge-connectivity is below (5/2)omega - 1 (omega the oddness), so the general statement is not reached by this result alone.

checked_by.qualification: Refereed journal publication (referee process not inspected)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (journal reference from arXiv page)

events.doubts: The constant is disputed between sources: the arXiv abstract page shows (5/2)omega - 1; a search summary of the PDF reported (5/2)omega - 3. I did not open the PDF to settle it.
events.direction: Restricted-class support; consistent with the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Mazzuoccolo and Steffen, 'Nowhere-zero 5-flows on cubic graphs with oddness 4', arXiv 1412.5398 (v1 17 Dec 2014; only version); published J. Graph Theory 85(2) (2017) 363-371 (search summary, journal not opened). Main theorem: every cyclically 6-edge-connected cubic graph with oddness at most 4 has a nowhere-zero 5-flow. The abstract states that by Kochol's reduction this is a step toward the whole statement. The arXiv abstract also gives the consequence that every minimum counterexample has oddness at least 6 (search summary).
events.revisions: v1 17 Dec 2014 only (per arXiv page); journal version J. Graph Theory 2017 (search summary).
events.delivers: Restricted class: cyclically 6-edge-connected cubic bridgeless graphs with oddness at most 4 have a nowhere-zero 5-flow. Via Kochol's reduction, a counterexample to the general statement would have oddness at least 6.
events.remains: Cyclically 6-edge-connected cubic graphs of oddness 6 or more. With Kochol's reduction, these are the remaining cases of the general statement that this result does not cover.

checked_by.who: Journal of Graph Theory (journal of record, 2017, per search summary)

events.direction: Restricted-class support; consistent with the conjecture. Its consequence (counterexamples must have oddness at least 6) narrows but does not close the search.

events.what_happened: Jacobsen and Salas, 'Is the five-flow conjecture almost false?', arXiv 1009.4062 (ID indicates September 2010). The paper concerns real zeros of the flow polynomial and disproves the Haggard-Pearce-Royle modification of Welsh's conjecture on real flow roots. It is about a different question with a similar name. Not opened; search snippet only.
events.delivers: A result about real roots of the flow polynomial (Welsh's question, a different problem from the existence of a nowhere-zero 5-flow). It establishes nothing about the existence statement.
events.direction: Does not bear on the statement; a different question sharing a name.

events.what_happened: Jiaao Li and Bo Su, 'Nowhere-zero 5-flows for graphs with bounded genus', Operations Research Transactions 29(3) (2025) 124-134, online 9 Sep 2025 (received 26 Feb 2025). The abstract (search-result text; the journal page was not opened because the host refused the connection) says: 'we show that every bridgeless graph of Euler genus at most 20 admits a nowhere-zero 5-flow, which improves several known results.' No arXiv preprint was found.
events.revisions: No arXiv or other earlier version found. The online date is the earliest public appearance I could find; the first written argument may be earlier and is not established.
events.delivers: Restricted class: every bridgeless graph of Euler genus at most 20 has a nowhere-zero 5-flow. This covers orientable surfaces up to genus 10 and nonorientable surfaces up to Euler genus 20 (my reading: Euler genus of orientable genus g is 2g). The class of all bridgeless graphs is not covered.
events.remains: Every bridgeless graph not embeddable in a surface of Euler genus at most 20 (that is, every bridgeless graph of Euler genus greater than 20), so the general statement stays open.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published online (received 26 Feb 2025, online 9 Sep 2025, per search summary)

events.doubts: Not read in full: the journal host refused the connection (ECONNREFUSED) and no arXiv copy was found, so the proof, the constant and the comparison with earlier results are unchecked. No critique or follow-up work was found in searches.
events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture in a restricted class (all graphs of bounded Euler genus); does not cut against it.

events.what_happened: Esperet, Lagoutte, Marseloo (v1 19 Dec 2025), joined by Hendrey, Norin and Steiner in v2 (21 Apr 2026), 'Nowhere-zero flow reconfiguration', arXiv 2512.17342. v1 conjectured 'that any two nowhere-zero 5-flows in any 2-edge-connected graph are connected in this way' (reconfiguration by changing one cycle at a time), which the abstract calls 'a reconfiguration variant of Tutte's 5-flow conjecture'. The v4 abstract says the natural reconfiguration variant of Tutte's 5-flow conjecture 'is false in the group and integer cases'. Theorem 3.4 (v4): there is a graph G with a nowhere-zero Z5-flow that forms an isolated vertex in the reconfiguration graph, giving a negative answer to Problem 1.1. The paper credits AlphaEvolve with finding that example (see ai).
events.revisions: v1 19 Dec 2025 (150 KB); v2 21 Apr 2026 (new results and new co-authors); v3 4 May 2026 (small correction in the proof of Theorem 6.22); v4 3 Jul 2026 (small corrections in Section 6.4).
events.delivers: Answers a different question: whether nowhere-zero 5-flows form a connected space under single-cycle moves. The reconfiguration analogue is answered negatively (Theorem 3.4), in group and integer settings. Positive results are for all nowhere-zero Z2^8-flows of 2-edge-connected graphs, planar 7-flows, and a general 'some integer k' statement. None of these is about whether a nowhere-zero 5-flow exists.
events.remains: The existence statement of the bullet is not touched: the paper neither proves nor refutes that every bridgeless graph has a nowhere-zero 5-flow.
events.directly_checkable: The example graph in Theorem 3.4 would be checkable by hand (a nowhere-zero Z5-flow and the isolation of the flow in the reconfiguration graph) but the graph was not read.
events.doubts: v1 posed the k=5 reconfiguration question as a conjecture; v2-v4 answer it negatively, so the v1 wording was superseded. v3 and v4 corrected two proofs (Theorem 6.22; Section 6.4); those corrections were not inspected in detail.
events.direction: Answers the reconfiguration analogue negatively. The paper's result is about connectivity of flow space; it does not bear on existence of a nowhere-zero 5-flow in either direction.
events.object: A graph G (size and construction not read) with a nowhere-zero Z5-flow that is an isolated vertex in the reconfiguration graph, so the flow space is disconnected; used to answer Problem 1.1 negatively. Existence in the sense of this bullet is not at issue.

systems.name: AlphaEvolve
systems.what_it_did: Helped find the example graph (Theorem 3.4 in v4) with a nowhere-zero Z5-flow that is an isolated vertex, which answers the reconfiguration analogue negatively. The authors credit it with finding 'such an example'. The text read was Section 3 of v4; whether the example is the same as Theorem 3.4 is my reading.
systems.basis_quote: with the generous help of Yuval Wigderson and Patryk Morawski and the tool AlphaEvolve [12] we managed to find such an example.

events.what_happened: Nikolay Ulyanov, 'Graph Puzzles II.1: Counterexamples to Jain's Second Unit Vector Flows Conjecture', arXiv 2603.23328 (single version, 24 Mar 2026). Jain's conjectures (as stated in the paper): Conjecture 1.1, every bridgeless graph has a flow into S2 (unit vectors); Conjecture 1.2, a map q from S2 to {+-1,...,+-4} with antipodal points opposite and equidistant great-circle triples summing to zero. The paper says that if both were true they would imply Tutte's 5-flow conjecture. It gives two point sets on S2, each requiring the values +-5 (no +-1..+-4 labelling exists, verified by SAT), so Conjecture 1.2 is false as stated. It says nothing about Conjecture 1.1.
events.revisions: Single version v1 (24 Mar 2026), per arXiv page.
events.delivers: Refutes Jain's second (S2 labelling) conjecture as stated. Because Jain's pair would imply Tutte's conjecture, the refutation removes that particular route. It does not refute the first conjecture, does not bear on whether every bridgeless graph has a nowhere-zero 5-flow, and does not claim to settle Tutte's conjecture.
events.remains: The whole statement; also Jain's first conjecture (S2 flows for bridgeless graphs), which the paper does not analyse.

machine_checked.system: SAT solver (PicoSAT / pycosat) for both counterexamples; Lean 4 with Mathlib bv_decide for the 50-point case only (author's claim)

events.directly_checkable: The two finite point sets on S2 with their great-circle triples and antipodal pairs are checkable by hand in principle; the impossibility of a +-1..+-4 labelling is a finite SAT instance (50-point: 200 variables, 19,765 clauses; 36-point: 144 variables, 6,710 clauses) that can be rerun from the repository. The repository README says only Counterexample 1 is formally verified in Lean; the Lean files' sorry status was not inspected.
events.doubts: Single author; no peer review; computer-verified rather than human-verified (except the Lean claim for one case). No reply or response from Jain or any other author was found. The statement of Jain's conjectures differs between sources: Ulyanov states Conjecture 1.1 for every bridgeless graph, while Houdrouge-Miraftab-Morin state Jain's Conjecture 2 for bridgeless cubic graphs. The counterexample is to the labelling conjecture under both wordings.
events.direction: Against Jain's second conjecture (the S2 labelling), as stated in the paper. Not against Tutte's 5-flow conjecture: the paper treats Tutte's statement as the implied conclusion of Jain's pair, and a refutation of one implying conjecture leaves the implied conjecture open.
events.object: Two point sets on the unit sphere S2 that each require the values +-5 in any labelling for the S2 nz5-flow map. (1) A 50-point set: an expansion of the 30-point icosidodecahedron set by 20 further points from intersecting small circles, giving 40 great-circle triples and 25 antipodal pairs; the impossibility of a +-1..+-4 labelling is SAT-verified (unsatisfiable), while a labelling with values +-1..+-6 exists. Explicit in the sense that the point set is constructed, not an existence proof. (2) A 36-point set built from square-root arithmetic with parameters v1=1, v2=3, w=2, reduced after pruning a 126-point component to 36 points and 13 triples; the +-1..+-4 labelling is SAT-refuted and a +-5 labelling exists. Both are explicit constructions.

events.what_happened: Hussein Houdrouge, Bobby Miraftab, Pat Morin, '2-dimensional unit vector flows', arXiv 2602.21526 (v1 25 Feb 2026; only version). The paper gives a geometric characterisation of S2-flows on cubic graphs, shows the class is closed under a composition operation and that vertex-to-triangle blow-ups preserve S2-flow existence, and proves (Theorem 3) that an S2-flow with rank at most 2 and odd-coordinate-free quotient gives a nowhere-zero 4-flow. It states Jain's Conjecture 2 for bridgeless cubic graphs and Conjecture 3 as the labelling, and says the two imply Tutte's conjecture. It poses Problem 1: whether S^d-flows give a nowhere-zero integer k-flow for some k at most 5 (open).
events.revisions: Single version v1 (25 Feb 2026), per arXiv page.
events.delivers: Structural results on S2-flows of cubic graphs and a sufficient condition for a nowhere-zero 4-flow. Nothing on the existence of a nowhere-zero 5-flow for general bridgeless graphs.
events.remains: The whole statement; also Jain's cubic S2-flow conjecture, which the paper does not settle.
events.doubts: Authors' own paper; no independent check found. Theorem 3 gives a 4-flow only under a rank and coordinate condition, so it does not transfer to 5-flows.
events.direction: Neutral to Jain's cubic S2-flow conjecture; no counterexample, no 5-flow result. Does not cut against Tutte's conjecture.

events.what_happened: Chenxing Li, Jiaao Li, Rong Luo, Bo Su, 'High-Dimensional p-Normed Flows', arXiv 2601.12036 (v1 17 Jan 2026; only version). Defines a flow index for d-dimensional p-normed nowhere-zero flows; proves phi_{2,p}(G) <= 3 and phi_{3,p}(G) <= 1+sqrt(2) for bridgeless graphs and tight bounds for graphs with a nowhere-zero 4-flow. Its introduction says it 'provide[s] supporting evidences for Tutte's 5-flow Conjecture and Jain's S2-Flow Conjecture'.
events.revisions: Single version v1 (17 Jan 2026), per arXiv page.
events.delivers: Upper bounds on a flow index for p-normed vector flows and equalities for graphs already having nowhere-zero 3- or 4-flows. No nowhere-zero 5-flow result for general bridgeless graphs; the paper calls its contribution supporting evidence and says it gives 'an approach to attack' the conjecture.
events.doubts: The paper itself describes its contribution as supporting evidence, not proof of the conjecture. The statement of supporting evidence is a claim by the authors, not an independent reading.
events.direction: Supporting evidence only (authors' description). Does not cut against the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Kathryn Nurse, 'Bouchet's conjecture for cyclically 5-edge-connected, cubic signed graphs', arXiv 2601.05692 (9 Jan 2026; one version). Proves Bouchet's 1983 conjecture that every flow-admissible signed graph has a nowhere-zero 6-flow, for cyclically 5-edge-connected cubic signed graphs. The introduction calls Bouchet's conjecture 'a signed graph analogue of Tutte's famous 5-flow conjecture'.
events.revisions: Single version v1 (9 Jan 2026), per arXiv page.
events.delivers: A result on signed graphs (6-flows, cyclically 5-edge-connected cubic), an analogue of the statement and not the statement itself. Settles nothing for unsigned bridgeless graphs.
events.direction: Analogue only; consistent with the conjecture's spirit but says nothing about unsigned 5-flows.

events.what_happened: Daniel Cranston, Jiaao Li, Bo Su, Zhouningxin Wang, Ningyan Xu, 'Reconfiguration of Nowhere-zero Flows', arXiv 2606.24685 (23 Jun 2026; one version). Defines A-flow-adjacency and A-flow-connectedness for nowhere-zero flows; characterises Z3- and 3-flow-connected graphs; shows all cubic bipartite graphs are Z4-flow-connected; conjectures Eulerian graphs are k-flow-connected for even k; shows 4-edge-connected graphs are A-flow-connected for |A| >= 5.3 x 10^6. Credits Esperet et al. with earlier results. It does not address the Esperet et al. k=5 question in the part read.
events.revisions: Single version v1 (23 Jun 2026), per arXiv page.
events.delivers: A different question: connectedness of flow space under A-adjacency. Nothing about existence of a nowhere-zero 5-flow in bridgeless graphs.
events.doubts: Only the first 100k of 148k characters was read; no AI statement appeared in the part read.
events.direction: Different question; does not bear on the statement in either direction.

events.what_happened: Robert Samal and Hadi Zamani, 'Typical properties of countable graphs: flows and bridges', arXiv 2609.28016 (23 Sep 2026; one version). Studies nowhere-zero flows in countably infinite graphs, distinguishing two kinds of bridge, and typical properties of countable graphs.
events.revisions: Single version v1 (23 Sep 2026), per arXiv page.
events.delivers: Results about infinite (countable) graphs. Does not address finite bridgeless graphs and does not mention Tutte's 5-flow conjecture.
events.remains: The whole statement, which concerns finite bridgeless graphs as the bullet is read; the infinite case is a different question.
events.doubts: Abstract page only; full text not read.
events.direction: Different question (countable graphs); does not bear on the statement.

events.what_happened: Chenxing Li, Jiaao Li, Rong Luo, Bo Su, 'Reduction Operations and Characterizations of S1-Flows in Graphs', arXiv 2608.18725 (v1 19 Aug 2026; v2 16 Sep 2026). Reduction techniques for S1-flows (circle-valued flows); characterises graphs with a spanning triangle-tree and triangularly connected graphs that admit S1-flows; shows that for maximum degree at most 4, a nowhere-zero 3-flow exists iff an S1-flow exists.
events.revisions: v1 19 Aug 2026; v2 16 Sep 2026 (no change in size noted).
events.delivers: Results on S1-flows and 3-flows for graphs of bounded maximum degree or special structure. Nothing on 5-flows for general bridgeless graphs. Does not mention Tutte's 5-flow or Jain's conjectures.
events.doubts: Abstract page only; full text not read.
events.direction: Different question; does not bear on the statement in either direction.

events.what_happened: OpenAI announced on 10 July 2026 (researcher Ethan Knight's X post, per search summary; the X page returned HTTP 402 and was not opened) a proof of the Cycle Double Cover Conjecture, credited to GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra, produced in just under an hour using 64 subagents. A PDF with the proof and the prompt was released on OpenAI's CDN (the PDF returned binary content through the fetcher and was not readable). Expositions followed: Geelen (arXiv 2607.15399, 16 Jul 2026, 'OpenAI's proof of the Cycle Double Cover Theorem'), Oum (arXiv 2607.16356, 17 Jul 2026; v2 23 Jul; v3 1 Aug 2026), and Carmesin (Matroid Union guest post, 21 Jul 2026, 'yes, the proof is correct'). OpenAI's cdc-lean repository's README claims a kernel-checked unconditional cycle double cover theorem for finite loopless bridgeless multigraphs, built on a formalised Jaeger-Kilpatrick eight-flow theorem. This is a different conjecture from Tutte's 5-flow statement. It is recorded because it is an AI-credited result in the same area, and because one expositor (Oum) states the link to the 5-flow conjecture.
events.revisions: OpenAI PDF released 10 Jul 2026 (announcement date per search summaries; Chinese outlets date it 11 Jul, Beijing time). Oum exposition v1 17 Jul, v2 23 Jul, v3 1 Aug 2026. Geelen note v1 16 Jul 2026 only.
events.delivers: A different question: every bridgeless (multi)graph has a cycle double cover (the Cycle Double Cover Conjecture, per the sources). It uses a nowhere-zero F2^3-flow from the eight-flow theorem and linear algebra. Oum's exposition states the orientable 5-cycle-double-cover conjecture (Archdeacon-Jaeger) would imply Tutte's 5-flow conjecture, and that this orientable conjecture is not proved by the paper. So the result does not reach the 5-flow statement.
events.remains: The whole 5-flow statement; the orientable 5-cycle-double-cover conjecture that would imply it remains open per Oum.

checked_by.qualification: Not established in the source beyond the guest-contributor label
checked_by.what_they_did: Stated 'yes, the proof is correct'; summarised how it was checked: Oum's talk and exposition, Geelen and Oum notes, and Lean 4 formalisations including one by OpenAI

checked_by.who: Sang-il Oum (exposition author; mathematician per search summary)
checked_by.qualification: Graph theorist (search summary places him at the Institute for Basic Science, Korea)
checked_by.what_they_did: Wrote an exposition presenting the proof with two modifications; the abstract says it is 'intended to make it more accessible' and does not state correctness

checked_by.qualification: Graph theorist (not verified in the source)
checked_by.what_they_did: Wrote a note to clarify the OpenAI proof: 'This write-up offers no new insights, but some people may find it easier to read.'

machine_checked.system: Lean 4 (OpenAI cdc-lean repository; README pins Lean v4.31.0)

events.doubts: No peer review found. The Lean claim (README) is unverified here; the repository's statement and sorry status were not shown. The 'machine-verified' wording in one aggregator is not confirmed. Thomas Bloom reportedly praised the proof but criticised the lack of citations (secondary report). Cun-Quan Zhang disputes the '50-year' framing (secondary report; not about correctness). Oum modified two steps in the exposition.
events.direction: Proves the Cycle Double Cover Conjecture (per the authors and expositors). Does not establish the 5-flow statement, and its link to the orientable 5-cycle-double-cover conjecture is stated by Oum as not proved.

events.what_happened: Yuta Inoue, Ken-ichi Kawarabayashi, Rintaro Matsuo, Atsuyuki Miyashita, Bojan Mohar, Tomohiro Sonobe, 'Three-edge-coloring apex cubic graphs', arXiv 2608.22870 (24 Aug 2026; one version). Proves that every 2-connected apex cubic graph is 3-edge-colourable, presented as completing the apex case of Tutte's three-edge-colouring conjecture. The proof is computer-assisted with source code (GitHub) and pseudocode. The abstract states that independent implementations reconstructed from the pseudocode, 'using generative AI systems', reproduced the computational results, and that 'These reconstructions are not part of the mathematical justification of the theorem'. The paper does not mention nowhere-zero flows or the 5-flow statement.
events.revisions: Single version v1 (24 Aug 2026), per arXiv page.
events.delivers: A different question: 3-edge-colourability of 2-connected apex cubic graphs (Tutte's three-edge-colouring conjecture, apex case). Says nothing about nowhere-zero 5-flows for bridgeless graphs. Connection to the Petersen-minor 4-flow sibling is made only in secondary sources, not in the paper's abstract.
events.directly_checkable: Computer-assisted: the authors give pseudocode and source code on GitHub; not checked.
events.doubts: Computer-assisted proof, not yet peer reviewed; the apex-case proof is described as 'if valid' in a secondary source. The generative-AI reproduction is stated by the authors to be outside the proof.
events.direction: A different question; does not bear on the 5-flow statement in either direction.

disputes.summary: The domain of Jain's unit-vector-flow conjecture differs between sources. Ulyanov (arXiv 2603.23328) states Conjecture 1.1 as every bridgeless graph has a flow into S2. Houdrouge, Miraftab and Morin (arXiv 2602.21526) state Jain's Conjecture 2 for bridgeless cubic graphs. The labelling conjecture (S2 nz5-flow) is stated the same way in both. The judging pass should read both wordings before relying on either.

The cyclic edge-connectivity constant in Steffen's 2006/2010 result is reported differently: the arXiv abstract page gives n >= (5/2)omega - 1; a search summary of the PDF gives (5/2)omega - 3. The PDF was not opened to settle it.

The date of Kochol's reduction (minimum counterexample is a cyclically 6-edge-connected cubic graph) is given as 2002, 2004 and 2006 by different secondary sources. Mazzuoccolo and Steffen (arXiv 1412.5398) cite 2004. The Kochol journal record was not opened (HTTP 503).

summary: What was found. Searches for the statement under its own name and under the names of the related conjectures (Tutte's 5-flow conjecture, the nowhere-zero 5-flow conjecture, and Jain's unit-vector-flow conjectures), plus the reconfiguration, Bouchet and cycle-double-cover neighbourhoods and AI-specific queries, found no proof, disproof, or counterexample of the statement since 26 January 2024. The Wikipedia Nowhere-zero flow article gives 'As of 2026, the following are currently unsolved (due to Tutte)' for the three conjectures; the Illinois open-problem page and the Mohar problem page (last updated 2003) state the conjecture without a resolution; the Matroid Union post, the Oum exposition, Ulyanov and Houdrouge et al. all describe the statement as open. In the window there are three kinds of event. (1) A restricted-class result: Li and Su (Operations Research Transactions, online 9 Sep 2025) show every bridgeless graph of Euler genus at most 20 has a nowhere-zero 5-flow. This is the one in-window event that settles a class of the statement. I could not open the journal page (connection refused), so the claim rests on the search-result abstract and no preprint was found; its first public written argument may predate the online date. Close call: whether a bounded-genus class counts as a restricted case of the bullet; I record it as a restricted case. (2) Route papers on Jain's conjectures, which are not restricted cases but partial work toward the statement: Li-Li-Luo-Su (Jan 2026) claim supporting evidence and bounds; Houdrouge-Miraftab-Morin (Feb 2026) give S2-flow structure and a 4-flow condition; Ulyanov (Mar 2026) gives computer-verified counterexamples to Jain's S2 labelling conjecture, which both sources say, together with Jain's first conjecture, would imply Tutte's 5-flow conjecture. Ulyanov's refutation removes one implying route; it is not a result about Tutte's statement and does not cut against it. Close call: a reader could take the implication as making the refutation bear on the bullet; I read it as no, since the implied statement is not refuted by refuting one implying conjecture. (3) Neighbouring problems, recorded separately because they carry AI credit or are close in name: the reconfiguration analogue (Esperet et al., Dec 2025, v4 Jul 2026), answered negatively with an example the authors credit to AlphaEvolve; the OpenAI cycle-double-cover proof (10 Jul 2026, credited to GPT 5.6), which is a different conjecture whose proof does not reach the 5-flow statement, by Oum's own account; Nurse's Bouchet analogue for signed graphs (Jan 2026); Inoue et al.'s apex cubic three-edge-colouring (Aug 2026), with generative AI used only to reproduce code; and three other 2026 papers on related flow notions (Cranston et al., Samal-Zamani, Li-Li-Luo-Su on S1-flows). Historic partial results are recorded as predates-window events: Kilpatrick/Jaeger 8-flows, Seymour's 6-flows, Steinberg's projective-plane case, Kochol's reductions and the cubic Petersen-minor-free case, Steffen's nonorientable-genus-5 case (title only) and cyclic-connectivity case, and Mazzuoccolo-Steffen's oddness-4 case. AI involvement in the 5-flow statement itself: none found in any source I read. AI credit appears only in neighbouring events: AlphaEvolve (reconfiguration example) and GPT 5.6 (cycle double cover). Several 2026 abstracts were read without full text, and this is flagged per event. The search for a Lean or formal record of the 5-flow statement found none; the only Lean material found concerns neighbouring results (OpenAI's cdc-lean, Ulyanov's counterexample). The parent bullet was read on the Wikipedia list page: 'Tutte's conjectures:' with sub-bullets for this statement and for Petersen-minor-free bridgeless graphs having a nowhere-zero 4-flow. Wikipedia's list page was read at a later revision (banner dated October 2026), so its wording may not match the 26 January 2024 frozen revision; the statement given to me was used as the authority.
competing_reading: The strongest case against my reading of the Li-Su result: the bound is on Euler genus, so it covers only bridgeless graphs embeddable in surfaces of bounded genus, a very thin slice of all bridgeless graphs. A judge who counts only results that settle the statement for all graphs would record no in-window event that settles the bullet. The strongest case for reading Ulyanov's refutation as bearing on the bullet: the Jain pair is presented as implying Tutte's conjecture, so a refutation of one implying conjecture might be read as taking away evidence for the implied one. I think that reading is weak, because the refutation does not contradict the implied statement, but it is the reading a judge is most likely to test. For the cycle-double-cover proof, the strongest case that it reaches the bullet is that Tutte's conjecture is implied by the orientable 5-cycle-double-cover conjecture and CDC is related to it; Oum's exposition explicitly says the orientable 5-cover conjecture is not proved, so I do not think it reaches the bullet.
what_would_settle_it: For Li-Su: the full text of the Operations Research Transactions paper (or an arXiv preprint) and an independent reading of the proof and the Euler-genus constant. For Ulyanov: the Lean file contents (sorry status) and an expert check of the SAT encodings; and whether Jain or another author responds. For the cycle double cover: the OpenAI PDF text, the cdc-lean statement and sorry audit, and a refereed publication. For the 5-flow statement: a general arXiv preprint claiming it, or the absence of one after the date of this record; the searches run to 11 Oct 2026 found none.

event.what_happened: Jiaao Li and Bo Su, 'Nowhere-zero 5-flows for graphs with bounded genus', Operations Research Transactions 29(3) (2025) 124-134, online 9 Sep 2025 (received 26 Feb 2025). The abstract (search-result text; the journal page was not opened because the host refused the connection) says: 'we show that every bridgeless graph of Euler genus at most 20 admits a nowhere-zero 5-flow, which improves several known results.' No arXiv preprint was found.
event.revisions: No arXiv or other earlier version found. The online date is the earliest public appearance I could find; the first written argument may be earlier and is not established.
event.delivers: Restricted class: every bridgeless graph of Euler genus at most 20 has a nowhere-zero 5-flow. This covers orientable surfaces up to genus 10 and nonorientable surfaces up to Euler genus 20 (my reading: Euler genus of orientable genus g is 2g). The class of all bridgeless graphs is not covered.
event.remains: Every bridgeless graph not embeddable in a surface of Euler genus at most 20 (that is, every bridgeless graph of Euler genus greater than 20), so the general statement stays open.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published online (received 26 Feb 2025, online 9 Sep 2025, per search summary)

event.doubts: Not read in full: the journal host refused the connection (ECONNREFUSED) and no arXiv copy was found, so the proof, the constant and the comparison with earlier results are unchecked. No critique or follow-up work was found in searches.
event.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture in a restricted class (all graphs of bounded Euler genus); does not cut against it.

events.ai_basis: with the generous help of Yuval Wigderson and Patryk Morawski and the tool AlphaEvolve [12] we managed to find such an example.
The proof presented in this note is due to GPT 5.6 announced by OpenAI [22] in July 2026.

judgement.why: The statement is a single universal claim, so restricted-class results (projective plane, bounded genus, cubic Petersen-minor-free, cyclic connectivity vs oddness, oddness 4) are cases, and the 8- and 6-flow theorems are bounds on the flow number. The only in-window event touching the statement itself is Li and Su (2025): Euler genus at most 20 is a restriction, so case; it was accepted by a refereed journal, which meets the digested bar even though the researcher read only the abstract. Ulyanov refutes an implying conjecture (Jain's labelling), which removes a route but neither settles nor bounds Tutte's statement: none. The Jain-route structural and p-normed papers are none. Reconfiguration, signed-graph, countable-graph, S1-flow, apex 3-edge-colouring and cycle double cover papers answer different questions: variant. AI roles were still answered per event: AlphaEvolve found the reconfiguration example in human-led work (assisted); GPT 5.6 is credited with the whole CDC proof (generated); Inoue et al.'s generative-AI reproduction is outside the proof (none). All three are variants and do not bear on this statement.
judgement.doubts: Li-Su rests on a search-result abstract; the full text was never read and the first public argument may predate the 9 Sep 2025 online date (still after the snapshot either way). Kochol and Steffen 1996 entries rest on search summaries and a title. The Kochol event bundles several results (1999 class result, a reduction, a girth bound) with unsettled dates; all are pre-snapshot.
